title: Seònaid gathers the first three witnesses
summary: At Queen Catrìona's own asking, her clerk Seònaid nic Coinnich takes down, in hurried hours snatched from the court's business, the first accounts of the war of the three claims: a soldier who fought at the ford, the son of Taigh na Fèithe's store-master, and a woman of Doire mhin who remembers Na Teallaichean Fuara as a child.

title: Seònaid visits the harbour-house boards
summary: Carrying a grant of harbour dues she did not need to carry in her own hand, Seònaid nic Coinnich asks the harbour scribe Ailean mac Mhurchaidh to show her the old boards of Rolla nan Deònach, and rides home with an errand for herself she had not had when she set out.

title: The store-master's board copied in full
summary: Dòmhnall mac Eòghainn, who inherited his father Eòghann mac Dhùghaill's office at Taigh na Fèithe's store, lets Seònaid nic Coinnich copy in full the board of shires refused the coal in the year of Na Teallaichean Fuara, a board his father kept face to the wall and never scraped clean.

title: The witness of Doire mhin heard in full
summary: Seònaid nic Coinnich rides to Cathair mhòr to hear Mairead nic Aonghais, a woman of Doire mhin who was a child in the same charity and at the same temple as Seònaid herself, tell at length what a cold hearth was to a child too young to be told why it was cold.

title: Seònaid weighs Leabhar a' Chùraim against her witnesses
summary: At Taigh na Fèithe Seònaid nic Coinnich sets her gathered testimony against Leabhar a' Chùraim's own entries of the war, and finds days, numbers and causes of death the book and the witnesses do not agree on; she resolves to keep both accounts rather than choose between them.

title: King Lachlann reads his mother into the book
summary: Lachlann mac Iain finds Seònaid nic Coinnich at work on her history and asks whether it will say what his mother Catrìona was like; she answers that it will say what she did and what was believed of her, which is the most any book can give.

title: Seònaid finishes Leabhar nan Trì Tagraichean
summary: Seònaid nic Coinnich writes the last of the war's telling and sets down the finished leaves, the first history on Dia-thìr told as one tale from end to end rather than as separate entries.

title: Death of Seònaid nic Coinnich
summary: Seònaid nic Coinnich dies at Cathair dhearg at two-and-eighty, seven years after finishing her book, her last recorded word a complaint that the harbour-house's back room at Seann Skell wants a better roof before the damp takes its oldest boards.

title: Leabhar nan Trì Tagraichean read at An Talla Dearg
summary: King Lachlann mac Iain has Seònaid nic Coinnich's finished history read into the record at An Talla Dearg and orders it copied again and kept, ruling that no later copy of it may ever be made shorter than the one before it.

title: Fearchar Ciar swears the ford broke on two days
summary: Where Leabhar a' Chùraim gives the breaking at the ford of Àth shean as one day, the old soldier Fearchar Ciar swears to Seònaid nic Coinnich that it was two, the fighting taken up again at first light after a night neither side thought worth entering.

title: Birth of the heir of Anna
summary: A child is born at Cathair dhearg to Anna, Lachlann mac Iain's daughter, then five-and-thirty years old; Clàr nan Rìghrean keeps the year of the birth and lets the child's name fall from every copy that survives.
